source_text: I. Cum esset persecutio sub Diocletiano et Maximiano imperatoribus, quando diversis agonibus concertantes Christiani, a tyrannis illata supplicia devota deo mente suscipientes, praemiis se perpetuis participes efficiebant. quod et factum est circa famulum dei Irenaeum episcopum urbis Sirmiensium, cuius iam nunc vobis certamen pandam victoriamque ostendam; qui pro modestia sua ingenita et timore divino, cui operibus rectis inserviebat, dignus nominis sui inventus est. II. Comprehensus itaque oblatus est Probo praesidi Pannoniae. Probus praeses dixit ad eum: Obtemperans praeceptis divinis sacrifica diis. Irenaeus episcopus respondit: Qui diis et non deo sacrificat eradicabitur. Probus praeses dixit: Clementissimi principes iusserunt aut sacrificare, aut tormentis succumbere debere. Irenaeus respondit: Mihi praeceptum est tormenta magis suscipere quam deum denegans daemoniis sacrificare. Probus praeses dixit: Aut sacrifica, aut faciam te torqueri. Irenaeus respondit: Gaudeo si feceris, ut domini mei passionibus particeps inveniar. Probus praeses iussit [eam — for eum?] vexari. cumque acerbissime vexaretur, dixit ad eum praeses: Quid dicis, Irenaee? sacrifica. Irenaeus respondit: Sacrifico per bonam confessionem deo meo, cui semper sacrificavi.
thought_title: Arrest and first refusal to offer sacrifice
orientation: Irenaeus, bishop of Sirmium, has been arrested and brought before Probus, governor of Pannonia, who orders him to offer sacrifice to the gods.
pass_a_gloss: When there was persecution under Diocletian and Maximian as emperors, when Christians striving in different contests, receiving with mind devoted to God the punishments brought upon them by tyrants, were making themselves sharers in lasting rewards. And this also happened in the case of Irenaeus, servant of God, bishop of the city of Sirmium, whose contest I will now lay open to you and whose victory I will show; who on account of his inborn modesty and divine fear, which he served with right works, was found worthy of his name. Having been seized therefore he was brought before Probus governor of Pannonia. Probus the governor said to him: Obeying the divine commands offer sacrifice to the gods. Irenaeus the bishop answered: Who offers sacrifice to gods and not to God will be rooted out. Probus the governor said: The most kind emperors have ordered that they must either offer sacrifice or yield to torture. Irenaeus answered: To me it is commanded rather to take up torture than denying God to offer sacrifice to evil spirits. Probus the governor said: Either offer sacrifice, or I will cause you to be tortured. Irenaeus answered: I rejoice if you do it, in order that I may be found a sharer in the sufferings of my Lord. Probus the governor ordered him to be violently handled. And when he was being violently handled most harshly, the governor said to him: What do you say, Irenaeus? Offer sacrifice. Irenaeus answered: I offer sacrifice through the good confession of faith to my God, to whom I have always offered sacrifice.

bible_refs.note: Qui diis et non deo sacrificat eradicabitur

pass_b_english: When persecution broke out under the emperors Diocletian and Maximian, Christians threw themselves into contests of many kinds. They accepted the punishments the tyrants inflicted on them with minds devoted to God, and so made themselves sharers in rewards that last forever. The same happened with Irenaeus, the servant of God and bishop of the city of Sirmium. I will now lay his contest before you and show you his victory. By his inborn modesty and his fear of God, which he served with upright deeds, he was found worthy of his name.

He was arrested and brought before Probus, the governor of Pannonia. The governor said to him, "In obedience to the divine commands, offer sacrifice to the gods." Bishop Irenaeus answered, "Whoever offers sacrifice to the gods and not to God shall be rooted out (Exodus 22:20)." The governor said, "Our most merciful emperors have ordered that you must either offer sacrifice or give way to torture." Irenaeus answered, "I have been commanded to undergo torture rather than to deny God and offer sacrifice to demons."

The governor said, "Either offer sacrifice, or I will have you tortured." Irenaeus answered, "I rejoice if you do it, so that I may be found sharing in the passion of my Lord." The governor ordered him to be violently handled. When he was being handled most cruelly, the governor said to him, "What do you say, Irenaeus? Offer sacrifice." Irenaeus answered, "I offer sacrifice to my God through a good confession of faith, and to Him I have always offered sacrifice."
notes: Source reads iussit eam vexari with editorial mark for eum; eam does not agree with Irenaeus; glossed as him following the correction.
